frame: Corrected GEO XYZ use the DLR SPG SHAP7 4M frame. A projective camera fitted from their pixel correspondences is checked against held-out pixels; surface transfer uses the public 124,938-face SHAP7 regional release. Independent native-pixel shape disagreements are retained in evidence/source-shape-comparison.json.

quality.radianceCompanion: Every decoded L4 radiance pixel must equal its L5 counterpart before the quality map is used.
quality.rejected: Missing VALID, bad, saturated, readout, nonlinear, shutter or reserved flags.
quality.interpretation: Bit 0 is positive VALID. The calibration-pipeline bit table and archived values take precedence over ambiguous all-zero wording in the science user guide. LOSSY is retained only for visual use.

photometry.description: Convert calibrated radiance to I/F using solar distance and solar flux from the original OSIRIS calibration HISTORY (pipeline section 3.13). Divide by the Lommel–Seeliger disk function and normalize the HG plus shadow-hiding phase terms to 50 degrees before interpolation. Phase parameters g=-0.37, B0=2.5 and h=0.079 are from Fornasier et al. (2015), Table 4, Hapke 2002 fit at 649 nm. This is a single-scattering approximation, not the full Hapke model or a measured albedo map.
photometry.applicationLighting: Uniform flood displays normalized imagery without directional model lights. Shadows applies the existing source-mesh fixed-epoch Sun recipe. Both banks are prepared.

manuals.purpose: Nine GEO planes, coordinates, angles and SHAP7 geometry.
Section 3.15.2: quality bits; Section 3.16: GEO generated from L4 radiance.
PDS plane layout, stored image orientation and image metadata.

limits: Eleven orange-filter observations from August 2014, October–November 2015 and April 2016 form a visual composite across changing illumination and a perihelion passage, not simultaneous color or albedo. No extrapolation or backside fill.

The public 125K SHAP7 and archival 4M SHAP7 are distinct resolutions. The transfer still requires every contributor within 20 m, emission within 80 degrees and independent visibility agreement within 0.5 m.

Photographed cast shadows, real seasonal surface changes and unmodeled scattering remain. The 1.3–54 degree published phase fit is extrapolated to older frames reaching 64 degrees; new frames are at 41–51 degrees.
Positive, zero and negative finite radiance are retained when validity/geometry/photometry permit.

mosaic.selection: Finest projected surface resolution among qualified observations, accounting for nadir pixel scale and emission angle. Source order breaks exact ties. Brightness never chooses an observation.
mosaic.levels: One bounded gain per observation from co-located positive samples with incidence and emission at most 65 degrees, at least 128 valid pairs and median level error at most 0.07. The first frame anchors the display; the residual-gain budget remains 1.35. Use 128 deterministic samples per retained triangle; an independent 127-sample grid changes all gains by less than 0.54%. Display keeps its original 80-degree limits.
mosaic.display: All selected surface samples supply the authored 1.9–99.3 percentile stretch. Encode the linearly stretched quantity to sRGB once for display.
mosaic.sourceIndex: The prepared lossless source-index raster records the winning observation at every atlas texel; zero marks no qualified observation.
